---
title: "How do I test whether a sample mean differs from a reference value?"
---

## What the question asks

How do I test whether a sample mean differs from a reference value?

## Steps in RStudio

1. Identify the reference mean and the sample observations.

2. Decide whether the question is two-sided or one-sided.

3. Run t.test(x,mu=...) and report the mean difference, interval, and p-value.

## Runnable example

```{r}
x <- c(10,12,11,15,14,13,12,16)
reference_mean <- 10
test <- t.test(x,mu=reference_mean,alternative="two.sided")
print(test$estimate)
print(test$conf.int)
print(test$p.value)
```

## Interpret the result

The two-sided test asks whether the population mean differs from 10 in either direction. Its p-value depends on the reference, sample, and assumptions.

## Check before using real data

A small p-value is not the size or importance of an effect. Assess assumptions and confidence interval.
